title: Custom Hook Testing
description: Learn strategies for testing custom hooks with React Testing Library and Jest.

data.text: Testing custom hooks is essential for maintaining reliable logic that is shared across components. React Testing Library provides utilities like `renderHook` and `act` that let you run hooks in a test environment, observe state changes, and assert behavior without rendering a full UI tree.

data.title: Testing a Simple useCounter Hook
data.content: Use renderHook to invoke the hook and access its result.

data.title: Why act() Matters
data.text: State updates in React are batched and flushed asynchronously. Wrapping imperative calls in act() ensures all updates are processed before assertions run.
Hooks that wrap async operations—such as data fetching or debouncing—require waiting for promises to resolve. Use `waitFor` to poll until the hook reaches the expected state.

data.title: Testing useAsync with waitFor
data.content: Assert loading, success, and error states in sequence.

data.text: Testing Hooks That Depend on Context
If a hook consumes React Context, `renderHook` accepts a `wrapper` option. Provide the context provider so the hook receives the values it expects.

data.title: Wrapping with a Context Provider
data.content: Testing a theme-aware hook inside a provider.

data.title: Common mocking patterns:
items: Use jest.spyOn to observe function calls inside the hook.
Replace window or document APIs with jest.spyOn for DOM-dependent hooks.
Create wrapper components that inject props to simulate parent behavior.
Avoid testing implementation details; assert on the returned state and callbacks.

data.title: Beware Over-Mocking
data.text: If you find yourself mocking every internal dependency, the hook may be doing too much. Consider splitting logic into smaller, testable units.

data.title: Test a useDebounce Hook
data.description: Write tests for a hook that delays updating a value.
steps: Create a useDebounce hook that takes a value and delayMs.
Test the initial state returns the original value.
Use jest.useFakeTimers() and act() to advance time.
Assert the debounced value updates only after the delay.
data.expectedOutcome: A fully tested debounce hook with mocked timers.

items.question: Should I test hooks independently or through components?
items.answer: Test hooks independently when they contain non-trivial logic. Thin wrappers around built-in hooks can be tested indirectly through components.

items.question: Why does my test fail with 'not wrapped in act()'?
items.answer: State updates are asynchronous. Wrap interactions in act() or use waitFor to let React flush pending updates before asserting.

data.title: Key Takeaways
points: renderHook executes a hook inside a test and returns its current result.
act() ensures all state updates are flushed before assertions.
waitFor handles async transitions by polling until the condition is met.
Context-dependent hooks need a wrapper provider in renderHook options.
data.takeaway: Testing hooks directly gives you fast, focused feedback on logic that components reuse.
